newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends steady, mid bonds slightly bid.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends steady, mid bonds slightly bid.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ debt ends flat, awaits U.S. data, CPI
* Expectation of further yield curve steepening helps mid bonds
New Zealand debt ended the week broadly unchanged after a quiet Friday session and dealers said the market's focus had turned to Tuesday's March quarter inflation data.
U.S. March retail sales and wholesale price data, due Friday night NZ time, might help set the scene for Monday's open but the NZ CPI remains the key data traders are watching for.

"Sure, everyone takes notice of the U.S. figures, so if the U.S. sells off we'll probably open up a touch weaker and if they get bid we'll open up a touch stronger in yield, but not a hell of a lot," one dealer said.
"The focus will still primarily be on the CPI."
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of 0.41 percent March quarter inflation (2.16 percent annually), against the Reserve Bank's expectation of 0.5 percent (2.2 percent).

Dealers expect a good quarterly out-turn to prompt an easing in monetary conditions closer to those assumed by the RBNZ in March. Most cite a 0.3 percent out-turn as bullish for short rates, although some suggest 0.4 percent might also prove capable of sparking a rally.
If the market fails to loosen conditions sufficiently the Reserve Bank is widely expected to attempt to ease them by reiterating that conditions are inappropriately firm.

The money market ended flat to slightly stronger on light flows. Expectations that the bond yield curve will steepen further are attracting dealers to the mid part of the curve, at the expense of the struggling longer maturities.
The 02/00s ended two basis points stronger at 8.09 percent while the 06s were one weaker at 8.23 percent.
